name: BeOne Medicines Ltd. (NASDAQ: ONC; HKEX: 06160; SSE: 688235)
analyst_actions: 2026-08-07 | Zacks Research | upgrade | Hold -> Strong Buy
product: Global oncology portfolio: BRUKINSA (zanubrutinib, BTK inhibitor) and BEQALZI (sonrotoclax, BCL2 inhibitor) in hematology, TEVIMBRA (tislelizumab, PD-1) and ZIIHERA (zanidatamab) in solid tumors, plus in-licensed Amgen products in China.
demand: Q2 2026 product revenue was $1,679,794 thousand, up 29% year over year; BRUKINSA reached $1.2B globally with US $893M up 31%; TEVIMBRA $229M up 18%; Amgen in-licensed products $157M up 25%. Guidance cites BRUKINSA US leadership and global expansion.
pricing_power: Gross margin improved to 90% from 87% on BRUKINSA mix and productivity, but the Aug 31 US agreement commits future FDA-approved products to pricing in line with other developed markets plus GENEROUS Medicaid rebates, and the 10-K warns MFN style pricing would cut US net revenue.
competition: The FY2025 10-K names BTK rivals AbbVie/Janssen IMBRUVICA, AstraZeneca CALQUENCE, Eli Lilly JAYPIRCA and InnoCare YINUOKAI; PD-1 rivals Merck KEYTRUDA, BMS OPDIVO, Roche TECENTRIQ; BCL2 rivals AbbVie/Roche VENCLEXTA and Ascentage lisaftoclax; and Nurix NX-5948 in BTK CDAC.
team: Co-founder John V. Oyler is Chairman and CEO; the Aug 5 release announced appointment of Felix J. Baker, Elizabeth F. Mooney and Charles L. Sawyers to the board; more than 12,000 employees globally including over 2,000 in the US; Baker Bros Advisors reported 7.8% ownership on Sep 16.
market_strategy: Shifting toward a US-centric integrated oncology company: onshore manufacturing investment above $1B at Hopewell NJ with a Section 232 tariff exemption, participation in the GENEROUS Medicaid model, defense of the BRUKINSA hematology franchise with sonrotoclax combinations, and solid tumor pipeline expansion via collaborations.
bull: Q2 2026 product revenue $1.68B up 29%, BRUKINSA $1.2B up 31% with US $893M up 31%, gross margin 90% vs 87%, FY26 guidance raised to $6.6-6.8B revenue and $1.0-1.1B GAAP operating income.
bear: Aug 31 US agreement commits future FDA approvals to developed-market pricing plus generous Medicaid rebates; 10-K warns MFN-style pricing cuts US net revenue. TEVIMBRA grew only 18%, opex guidance raised, insiders sold Sep 10-11.
falsifier: Q3 2026 US BRUKINSA net revenue below $893M quarterly run rate, or FY26 revenue guidance cut below $6.6B, reported on the Q3 2026 earnings date.
web_what_changed: Q2 2026 results on Aug 5 with FY26 guidance raised to $6.6-6.8B revenue and $1.0-1.1B GAAP operating income; Jun 30 BRUKINSA Phase 3 MANGROVE win in 1L MCL; Jul 23 US manufacturing investment above $1B; Aug 10 Revolution Medicines collaboration; Aug 25 FDA approval of a TEVIMBRA regimen in 1L HER2+ GEA; Aug 31 voluntary US government access and tariff agreement.
web_not_known_yesterday: Not found. No company disclosure dated 2026-09-24 or 2026-09-25. Latest dated items: Sep 22 Weiss Ratings upgrade to Hold (aggregator) and Sep 16 Baker Bros Advisors Schedule 13D/A reporting 7.8% ownership (primary). Shares closed 2026-09-24 at $359.97, down 1.38%.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Volume and mix, not price. Q2 2026 product revenue $1.68B, up 29%; BRUKINSA $1.2B, up 31% with US $893M up 31%; TEVIMBRA $229M up 18%; Amgen in-licensed $157M up 25%. Gross margin rose to 90% from 87% on proportionally higher global BRUKINSA mix and productivity cost savings. Guidance credits US BRUKINSA leadership and global expansion.
web_suppliers: In-house small molecule Suzhou and biologics Guangzhou (about 65,000 liters) plus a limited number of third-party CMOs and CROs; named commercial supply agreements with Boehringer Ingelheim Biopharmaceuticals China for TEVIMBRA and Catalent for BRUKINSA. The FY2025 10-K says safety stock is maintained and no supply disruption is anticipated; the Hopewell NJ expansion adds small molecule capacity.
web_customers: Distribution concentrated. FY2025 sales to the three largest distributors were ASD Specialty Healthcare (Cencora) 18.5%, McKesson 17.5% and Shanghai Pharmaceutical 10.1% of product revenue, together about 37.1% of trade receivables, per the FY2025 10-K filed 2026-02-26.
web_who_loses: Per the FY2025 10-K competitor table: AbbVie and Janssen IMBRUVICA, AstraZeneca CALQUENCE, Eli Lilly JAYPIRCA and InnoCare YINUOKAI in BTK; Merck KEYTRUDA, BMS OPDIVO, Roche TECENTRIQ and AstraZeneca IMFINZI in PD-1; AbbVie and Roche VENCLEXTA plus Ascentage lisaftoclax in BCL2; Nurix NX-5948 in BTK CDAC.
web_contradicting_evidence: Price risk is the core disconfirming item: the Aug 31 US agreement commits BeOne to price future FDA approvals in line with other developed markets and to GENEROUS Medicaid rebates, while the FY2025 10-K warns MFN style reference pricing would cut US net revenue. TEVIMBRA grew only 18% versus 31% for BRUKINSA; FY26 opex guidance was raised to $4.8-5.0B; insiders sold stock Sep 10-11; consensus target implies only about 12% upside.
web_if_management_right: FY2026 revenue of $6.6-6.8B, GAAP operating income $1.0-1.1B and non-GAAP $1.7-1.8B on about 118M diluted ADS, plus a possibly material reversal of tax valuation allowances. Second-half 2026: BRUKINSA 1L MCL regulatory submissions in the US, Europe, China and Japan; Tacabrutideg Phase 2 submission; BG-C9074 and BGB-B2033 Phase 3 starts. No future dated event is posted on the IR site.
web_if_management_wrong: US realized price breaks first if GENEROUS and MFN style commitments compress net price per patient on the roughly $893M quarterly US BRUKINSA run rate; next is CLL share, where sonrotoclax must displace VENCLEXTA based regimens. Expense growth (GAAP R&D +17%, SG&A +10%) outrunning revenue, single source CMO dependence and concentrated distributor receivables would amplify a miss.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: CDMOs Catalent for BRUKINSA and Boehringer Ingelheim for TEVIMBRA; distributors Cencora/ASD Specialty, McKesson and Shanghai Pharmaceutical; Royalty Pharma as royalty counterparty whose interest amortization sits in guidance; collaboration partners Amgen, Novartis, Revolution Medicines and Huahui Health; and Hopewell NJ suppliers as US investment passes $1B.
